It is essential to monitor patients closely for statin-related adverse reactions, including but not limited to elevated liver enzyme levels, myopathy, and rhabdomyolysis. The daily dosage of statins should be limited as recommended. 2. Rabeprazole increases the level or effect of resmetirom through mechanisms that require further clarification. Patients should be monitored closely. 3. When using moderate CYP2C8 inhibitors, the dose of resmetirom (a CYP2C8 substrate) should be reduced, and therapy should be closely monitored. Resmetirom may increase the level or effect of repaglinide, requiring careful observation. 4. Resmetirom, as a weak CYP2C8 inhibitor, may increase systemic exposure to sensitive CYP2C8 substrates. Caution is advised, and monitoring is necessary. 5. Rifampin significantly increases the level or effect of resmetirom. Alternative therapies should be considered to avoid serious interactions. 6. Co-administration of resmetirom (an OATP1B1/3 substrate) with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors should be avoided. Alternative drugs are recommended. 7. Ritonavir increases the level or effect of resmetirom. Serious interactions may occur, and alternative therapies should be used. 8. Rosiglitazone increases the level or effect of resmetirom. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 9. Resmetirom increases the level or effect of rosuvastatin. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 10. Rucaparib increases the level or effect of resmetirom. Serious interactions may occur, and alternative drugs should be used. 11. Seladelpar levels may increase when co-administered with resmetirom. Adverse effects should be monitored if BCRP inhibitors are used concurrently. 12. Selpercatinib increases the level or effect of resmetirom. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 13. Simvastatin levels or effects may increase with resmetirom. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are required. 14. Tamoxifen increases the level or effect of resmetirom. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 15. Teriflunomide increases the level or effect of resmetirom. Therapy adjustments and close monitoring are necessary. 16. Trimethoprim increases the level or effect of resmetirom. Therapy should be modified, and patients should be monitored closely. 17. Tucatinib levels or effects may increase with resmetirom. Caution is advised, and monitoring is necessary. 18. Velpatasvir increases the level or effect of resmetirom. Serious interactions may occur, and alternative drugs should be used. 19. Voxilaprevir increases the level or effect of resmetirom. Serious interactions may occur, and alternative drugs should be used. 20. During organogenesis, doses of resmetirom five times the maximum recommended level were associated with maternal toxicity in animal studies. However, no embryofetal effects were observed at lower, better-tolerated doses in pregnant rabbits. Similarly, no embryofetal developmental effects were observed in pregnant rats treated with the metabolite MGL-3623. 21. A preand postnatal development study in rats showed that maternal dosing of resmetirom during organogenesis through lactation resulted in decreased birth weight, increased stillbirths, and higher mortality rates (postnatal days 1–4) at 37 times the maximum recommended dose. 22. There is no information regarding the presence of resmetirom in human or animal milk, its effects on breastfed infants, or its impact on milk production. 23. Controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk, making the drug generally acceptable for use during pregnancy. 24. Resmetirom can be administered with or without food. It should be stored at 20–25°C (68–77°F), with permissible excursions to 15–30°C (59–86°F). 25. Adding plans allows for comparison of formulary status with other drugs in the same class.
